# Coolify Documentation

> Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Heroku, Vercel, Netlify and Railway, also available as Coolify Cloud

## Overview

- [Home](https://coolify.io/docs): Install Coolify on your own server, deploy apps from Git, run databases and 300+ one-click services. Guides for self-hosted and Coolify Cloud.

## Get Started

- [Choose your path](https://coolify.io/docs/choose-your-path): Decide between self-hosted Coolify and Coolify Cloud based on your goals, responsibilities, and operational comfort level.
- [Start with Self-hosted](https://coolify.io/docs/start-with-self-hosted): Install self-hosted Coolify on your own server with one command, or set it up manually. Server requirements, supported OS, Raspberry Pi and first login.
- [Start with Coolify Cloud](https://coolify.io/docs/start-with-cloud): Start with Coolify Cloud using your own servers while the Coolify team manages the Coolify instance for you.
- [Deploy your first app](https://coolify.io/docs/deploy-your-first-app): Deploy your first application on Coolify using the Docker Image option with a simple nginx example.
- [Deploy your first database](https://coolify.io/docs/deploy-your-first-database): Deploy your first Redis database on Coolify using the one-click resources list and test the connection from terminal.
- [Deploy your first service](https://coolify.io/docs/deploy-your-first-service): Deploy your first one-click service on Coolify using Umami and sign in to verify it is running.

## Resources

- [Product UI](https://coolify.io/docs/screenshots)
- [Sponsors](https://coolify.io/docs/sponsors): Meet the companies and organizations sponsoring Coolify development including hosting, infrastructure, and developer-tool partners.
- [Offers](https://coolify.io/docs/offers): Offers, credits, and partner resources for Coolify users.
- [Support](https://coolify.io/docs/support): Find the right place to ask for Coolify help and what to include so people can help faster.
- [Team](https://coolify.io/docs/team): Meet the international team developing Coolify including founder Andras Bacsai, core developers, community leads, and documentation maintainers.
- [Videos](https://coolify.io/docs/videos): Watch community video tutorials on Coolify self-hosted PaaS including installation, deployment, and complete walkthroughs for beginners.

## Contribute

- [Guidelines](https://coolify.io/docs/contribute/guidelines)
- [Coolify Core](https://coolify.io/docs/contribute/coolify)
- [Documentation](https://coolify.io/docs/contribute/documentation)
- [Service Templates](https://coolify.io/docs/contribute/service)

## Core / Understand Coolify

- [What is Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/what-is-coolify): Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Heroku, Vercel and Netlify. Deploy apps, databases and services to any server you own over SSH.
- [How Coolify works](https://coolify.io/docs/core/how-coolify-works): How the Coolify instance, connected servers, Docker, and reverse proxies work together.
- [Self Hosted vs Coolify Cloud](https://coolify.io/docs/core/selfhosted-cloud-comparison): Compare self-hosted Coolify and Coolify Cloud by ownership, responsibilities, and cost.
- [Build and Deployment Model](https://coolify.io/docs/core/build-deployment-model): How Coolify builds or pulls application images and replaces running containers on connected servers.
- [Docker and Containers](https://coolify.io/docs/core/docker-and-containers): How Docker images, containers, persistent storage, networks, and Compose fit into a Coolify deployment.
- [Networking in Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking-in-coolify): How public traffic, reverse proxies, Docker networks, and direct ports fit together in Coolify.
- [Security Model](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security-model): Understand Coolify's security boundary, built-in controls, and the infrastructure and workloads you must secure.

## Core / Manage Coolify / Instance Management

- [Instance settings](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/instance-settings): Configure self-hosted Coolify instance settings for URL, access, updates, backups, email, authentication.
- [Instance Environment Variables](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/environment-variables): Configure PHP memory, workers, and scheduled job dispatch for a self-hosted Coolify instance and apply environment changes.
- [Update Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/update): Update a self-hosted Coolify instance from the dashboard or terminal, and configure automatic updates.
- [Migrate realtime services to Reverb](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/reverb-migration): Prepare a self-hosted Coolify instance for the migration from the separate Soketi container to Laravel Reverb in the Coolify container.
- [Update Coolify Database](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/update-coolify-database): Update or roll back the internal PostgreSQL database used by a self-hosted Coolify instance.
- [Downgrade Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/downgrade): Return a self-hosted Coolify instance to an earlier release from the terminal, with backup and recovery safeguards.
- [Uninstall Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/instance-management/uninstallation): Remove a self-hosted Coolify instance or Coolify Cloud services from connected servers.

## Core / Manage Coolify / Backup and Recovery

- [Back up Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/instance-backup): Create and verify self-hosted Coolify instance backups, save the instance encryption key, and configure recurring backups.
- [Restore Coolify](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/instance-restore): Restore a self-hosted Coolify instance on the same machine or move it to a replacement machine.
- [Reset Root Password](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/reset-root-password): Recover access to a self-hosted Coolify instance by resetting the root account password from the server terminal.
- [Change Root Email](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/change-root-email): Recover access to a self-hosted Coolify instance by changing the root account login email from the server terminal.
- [Reset 2FA](https://coolify.io/docs/core/backup-and-recovery/reset-2fa): Recover access to a self-hosted Coolify account by clearing its two-factor authentication setup from the server terminal.

## Core / Persistent Storage / Storage mounts

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/persistent-storage/storage-mounts/overview): Understand how persistent storage keeps application and database data outside replaceable containers and choose the correct mount type in Coolify.
- [Volume mounts](https://coolify.io/docs/core/persistent-storage/storage-mounts/volume-mounts): Add a named Docker volume to a Coolify application or database and verify that its data survives redeployments.
- [Bind mounts](https://coolify.io/docs/core/persistent-storage/storage-mounts/bind-mounts): Map a specific directory on a Coolify deployment server into an application or database container.
- [File mounts](https://coolify.io/docs/core/persistent-storage/storage-mounts/file-mounts): Mount one Coolify-managed file or an existing host file at an exact path inside a container.
- [Backup](https://coolify.io/docs/core/persistent-storage/storage-mounts/backups): Schedule local and S3 backups for application volume and directory mounts, set retention, and verify each execution.

## Core / Persistent Storage / S3 Storage

- [S3 Storage Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/s3-storage/overview): Configure S3-compatible storage for Coolify backups with Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Neon Object Storage, Supabase Storage, and other supported providers.
- [Amazon S3](https://coolify.io/docs/core/s3-storage/aws): Connect Amazon S3 to Coolify by creating a bucket, IAM policy, IAM user, and access key.
- [Cloudflare R2](https://coolify.io/docs/core/s3-storage/r2): Configure Cloudflare R2 S3-compatible storage for Coolify backups with bucket creation, API token setup, and access credentials.
- [Neon Object Storage](https://coolify.io/docs/core/s3-storage/neon): Configure Neon Object Storage as an S3-compatible backup destination using your branch endpoint, bucket, region, and access keys.
- [Supabase Storage](https://coolify.io/docs/core/s3-storage/supabase): Configure Supabase Storage as an S3-compatible backup destination using your project endpoint, bucket, region, and access keys.

## Core / Infrastructure / Servers

- [Servers Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/overview): Understand server roles in Coolify and choose the right way to add, provision, and manage a server.
- [Add Server](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/add-server): Connect an existing Linux server to Coolify with SSH and prepare it for deployments.
- [Provision Cloud Server](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/provision-cloud-server): Purchase and create a Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, or Hostinger server from the Coolify dashboard.
- [Manage Server](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/manage-server): Update a connected server's connection, domain, timezone, build role, and cloud-provider link.
- [Remove Server](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/remove-server): Remove a server from Coolify, optionally delete its resources, and understand provider deletion.
- [OpenSSH](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/openssh): Configure OpenSSH for the localhost server or a remote server connected to Coolify.
- [Firewall](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/firewall): Open the firewall ports required by Coolify, its proxy, connected servers, and dashboard features.
- [Non-root User](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/non-root-user): Create a non-root SSH user and give it the access Coolify needs to manage a server.
- [Build Servers](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/build-servers): Add a dedicated build server and configure an application to use it for Docker image builds.
- [GitHub Actions Runners](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/github-actions-runners): Run GitHub Actions workflow jobs of an organization on your Coolify build servers, in ephemeral Docker containers.
- [Server Patching](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/server-patching): Check for operating-system package updates and install selected updates from the Coolify dashboard.
- [Docker Images](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/docker-images): Inspect Docker image disk usage and remove unused images from a server.
- [Automated Docker Cleanup](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/automated-docker-cleanup): Configure scheduled Docker cleanup and safely remove unused images, volumes, and networks from a server.
- [Web Terminal](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/servers/web-terminal): Open a browser terminal for a server or container and enable or disable terminal access for a server.

## Core / Infrastructure / Scaling

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/scaling/overview): Understand the scaling options available for applications deployed with Coolify and choose when to add servers or a cloud load balancer.
- [Multi-server Deployments](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/scaling/multi-server-deployments): Deploy one Coolify application to multiple standalone servers by using a shared Docker image and registry.
- [Cloud Load Balancing](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/scaling/cloud-load-balancing): Put a provider-managed load balancer in front of an application deployed by Coolify to multiple servers.
- [Docker Swarm (Deprecated)](https://coolify.io/docs/core/infrastructure/scaling/docker-swarm): Understand the Docker Swarm deprecation in Coolify and the requirements for maintaining an existing Coolify v4 deployment.

## Core / Networking / Destinations

- [Destinations Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/destinations/overview): Understand how Coolify uses Docker network destinations to deploy resources on your servers.
- [Create a Destination](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/destinations/create): Create another Docker network destination in Coolify or scan a network that already exists on a server.
- [Manage Destinations](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/destinations/manage): Review resources, rename destinations, select deployment networks, and clone resources to another destination.
- [Delete Destination](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/destinations/delete): Safely remove a destination and its Docker network after reviewing every attached resource.

## Core / Networking

- [Domains](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/domains): Configure domains, HTTPS, target ports, paths, redirects, search engine indexing, and generated domains for Coolify applications and services.
- [DNS](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/dns): Point domains to Coolify servers, verify DNS records, and configure wildcard domains and DNS validation.

## Core / Networking / Proxy

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/overview)

## Core / Networking / Proxy / Traefik

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/overview)
- [Update Traefik](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/update): Review Traefik release notes, change the proxy image version in Coolify, and restart the proxy.
- [Basic Authentication](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/basic-auth): Protect Coolify applications and Docker Compose services with Traefik HTTP basic authentication.
- [TLS Certificates](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/tls-certificates): Manage Traefik ACME certificates and restore backups of acme.json.
- [Custom SSL Certificates](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/custom-ssl-certs): Load certificates from a Coolify server into Traefik with dynamic configuration.
- [Dashboard](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/dashboard): Expose the Traefik dashboard through a dedicated authenticated domain in Coolify.
- [Custom Middlewares](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/custom-middlewares): Add reusable Traefik request middleware and redirects to Coolify resources.
- [Dynamic Configuration](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/dynamic-config): Add file-based Traefik routers, services, middleware, and TLS settings through Coolify.
- [Load Balancing](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/load-balancing): Route one Traefik domain to multiple reachable upstream servers or containers.
- [DNS Challenge](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/dns-challenge): Configure Traefik to obtain Let's Encrypt certificates through a DNS provider API.
- [Wildcard Certificates](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/wildcard-certs): Request and use a Traefik certificate that covers an apex domain and its subdomains.
- [Protect with Authentik](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/traefik/protect-services-with-authentik): Add Authentik forward authentication to Coolify resources through Traefik middleware.

## Core / Networking / Proxy / Caddy

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/caddy/overview)
- [Basic Authentication](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/caddy/basic-auth): Protect Coolify applications with Caddy HTTP basic authentication.
- [Custom SSL Certificates](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/caddy/custom-ssl-certs): Mount your certificate and private key into Coolify's Caddy proxy and configure the resource's TLS label.
- [DNS Challenge](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/caddy/dns-challenge): Build Caddy with a DNS provider module and use DNS-based ACME validation in Coolify.

## Core / Networking / Proxy / Custom

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/custom/overview)
- [NGINX](https://coolify.io/docs/core/networking/proxy/custom/nginx): A case study of how ShadowArcanist replaced Traefik with a hand-configured NGINX stack, with the configuration snippets behind it.

## Core / Team Management / Members

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/members/overview): Understand how team membership controls access to team-scoped resources and choose the right member management task.
- [Add a Member](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/members/add-a-member): Invite a person to a Coolify team by email or with a generated invitation link.
- [Remove a Member](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/members/remove-a-member): Remove a person from a Coolify team without deleting their account or the team's resources.
- [Delete a User](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/members/delete-user): Delete a user account from a self-hosted Coolify instance, with automatic team ownership transfer and resource cleanup rules.
- [Manage Members](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/members/manage-members): Review a Coolify team, change member roles, and manage pending invitations.

## Core / Team Management

- [Roles & Permissions](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/roles-and-permissions): Compare Owner, Admin, and Member access across team management, resources, servers, credentials, and API tokens.
- [Shared Variables](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/shared-variables): Create team, project, environment, and server-scoped values and reference them in Coolify resource configuration.
- [Audit Log](https://coolify.io/docs/core/team/audit-log): Search team activity and review resource changes in Coolify's audit log.

## Core / Security / Authentication / OAuth

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/overview): Understand OAuth sign-in behavior in Coolify and choose a provider-specific setup guide.
- [GitHub](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/github): Configure GitHub OAuth sign-in for Coolify by creating an OAuth App and registering the Coolify callback URL.
- [GitLab](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/gitlab): Configure GitLab.com or self-managed GitLab OAuth sign-in for Coolify with a read-user application.
- [Google](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/google): Configure Google OAuth sign-in for Coolify with a web OAuth client and the Coolify callback URL.
- [Azure](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/azure): Configure Microsoft Entra ID OAuth sign-in for Coolify with an app registration, tenant ID, and client secret.
- [Bitbucket](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/bitbucket): Configure Bitbucket Cloud OAuth sign-in for Coolify with an OAuth consumer and email permission.
- [Discord](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/discord): Configure Discord OAuth sign-in for Coolify with a Discord application and registered redirect URI.
- [Infomaniak](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/oauth/infomaniak): Configure Infomaniak OAuth sign-in for Coolify with an Application credential and callback URL.

## Core / Security / Authentication / SSO

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/sso/overview): Configure centralized Coolify sign-in with OpenID Connect, Authentik, Clerk, or Zitadel.
- [OpenID Connect](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/sso/oidc): Connect an OpenID Connect identity provider to Coolify and control account creation.
- [Authentik](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/sso/authentik): Configure Authentik SSO for Coolify with an OAuth2/OpenID Connect provider, application, and base URL.
- [Clerk](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/sso/clerk): Configure Clerk SSO for Coolify by creating a Clerk OAuth application and using its Frontend API URL.
- [Zitadel](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/sso/zitadel): Configure Zitadel SSO for Coolify with a confidential web application, client secret, and instance base URL.

## Core / Security / Authentication

- [2FA](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/2fa): Configure two-factor authentication, save recovery codes, and manage 2FA for a Coolify account.
- [Profile and Account Deletion](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/authentication/profile): Manage your Coolify profile, linked identity, and account deletion.

## Core / Security / Credentials

- [SSH Keys](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/credentials/ssh-keys): Create, authorize, rotate, and remove the SSH keys Coolify uses for servers and private Git repositories.
- [Cloud Tokens](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/credentials/cloud-tokens): Create and manage the Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, and Hostinger credentials Coolify uses for cloud servers.
- [Cloud-Init Scripts](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/credentials/cloud-init-scripts): Create reusable cloud-init YAML for Hetzner, DigitalOcean, and Vultr server provisioning.
- [API Tokens](https://coolify.io/docs/core/security/credentials/api-tokens): Create, scope, store, rotate, and revoke Coolify API tokens for integrations and automation.

## Core / Observability / Monitoring

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/monitoring/overview): Understand how Coolify monitors server availability, container state, disk usage, backups, and CPU and memory metrics.
- [Sentinel](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/monitoring/sentinel): Configure and troubleshoot Coolify Sentinel for server health, container status, disk usage, and metrics collection.
- [Metrics](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/monitoring/metrics): Enable and view Coolify CPU and memory metrics for servers, applications, and standalone databases.
- [Traffic Analytics](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/monitoring/traffic-analytics): Enable proxy traffic analytics for Traefik and Caddy and configure collection and retention.

## Core / Observability / Log Drains

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/log-drains/overview): Understand how Coolify forwards application, database, and service container logs to an external destination.
- [Axiom](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/log-drains/axiom): Send Coolify application, database, and service container logs to an Axiom dataset.
- [New Relic](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/log-drains/new-relic): Send Coolify application, database, and service container logs to New Relic Logs.
- [Custom Fluent Bit](https://coolify.io/docs/core/observability/log-drains/custom-fluent-bit): Configure Coolify to forward resource container logs with a complete custom Fluent Bit configuration.

## Core / Notifications

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/overview): Understand how Coolify sends team notifications through email, Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost, Pushover, and webhooks.
- [Notification Events](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/events): Choose which deployment, backup, scheduled task, container, and server events Coolify sends through each notification channel.

## Core / Notifications / Notification Channels

- [Email](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/email): Configure Coolify email notifications with hosted email, self-hosted instance-wide transactional email, SMTP, or Resend.
- [Discord](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/discord): Send Coolify notifications to a Discord channel through an incoming webhook.
- [Telegram](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/telegram): Configure a Telegram bot, chat, and optional topic IDs for Coolify notifications.
- [Slack & Mattermost](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/slack-mattermost): Send Coolify notifications to Slack or Mattermost through a Slack-compatible incoming webhook.
- [Pushover](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/pushover): Send Coolify push notifications through a Pushover application.

## Core / Notifications / Notification Channels / Webhook Notifications

- [Setup](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/webhook/setup): Configure Coolify to send notification events as JSON POST requests to an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint.
- [Payload Reference](https://coolify.io/docs/core/notifications/channels/webhook/payload-reference): Reference for Coolify webhook notification event identifiers, JSON fields, optional values, and example payloads.

## Core / Automation / Scheduled Tasks

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/scheduled-tasks/overview): Understand how Coolify runs scheduled commands inside application and service containers.
- [Create a Task](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/scheduled-tasks/create-a-task): Create a scheduled command for a Coolify application or service and verify its first execution.
- [Manage Tasks](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/scheduled-tasks/manage-tasks): Update, enable, disable, run, and delete scheduled tasks in Coolify.
- [Execution History](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/scheduled-tasks/execution-history): Read scheduled task status, timing, output, and downloadable logs in Coolify.

## Core / Automation / Tags

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/tags/overview): Group Coolify applications and services with team-scoped tags for filtering and bulk deployment.
- [Manage Tags](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/tags/manage-tags): Create, assign, reuse, and remove tags from Coolify applications and services.
- [Deploy by Tag](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/tags/deploy-by-tag): Redeploy a group of Coolify applications and services from the dashboard or a tag webhook.

## Core / Automation

- [Deploy Webhooks](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/deploy-webhooks): Trigger Coolify resource or tag deployments from CI and external automation with an authenticated webhook URL.
- [Cron Syntax](https://coolify.io/docs/core/automation/cron-syntax): Write five-field cron expressions and use Coolify's supported named schedules.

## Applications

- [Applications](https://coolify.io/docs/applications): Understand, deploy, configure, and operate applications with Coolify.

## Applications / Understand Applications

- [What is an application](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/what-is-an-application): Understand what an application is in Coolify and what you need before deploying one.
- [How Applications Work](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/how-applications-work): Follow how Coolify turns application source or an existing image into running Docker containers.
- [Choose a Deployment Method](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/choose-deployment-method): Choose whether Coolify deploys a Git repository, a Dockerfile entered without Git, a Git-based Docker Compose definition, or an existing image.
- [Coming from Managed Platforms](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/coming-from-managed-platforms): Map managed deployment platform concepts to Coolify, Docker, and servers you control.

## Applications / Source Code

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/overview): Choose how Coolify accesses a public or private Git repository.
- [Public Repositories](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/public-repositories): Deploy a public Git repository without creating a Git source or deploy key.
- [Deploy Keys](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/deploy-keys): Give Coolify read-only SSH access to one private Git repository.
- [Cursor Origin](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/cursor-origin): Deploy a private Cursor Origin repository with Coolify by sharing a deploy key between Coolify and Origin.
- [GitLab](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/gitlab): Deploy public and private GitLab repositories with a GitLab App, deploy key, or repository URL.
- [Bitbucket](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/bitbucket): Deploy Bitbucket repositories and configure repository and pull-request webhooks.
- [Gitea](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/gitea): Deploy Gitea repositories and configure push and pull-request webhooks.
- [Other Git Providers](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/other-providers): Deploy from another Git-compatible provider with public HTTPS access or an SSH deploy key.

## Applications / Source Code / GitHub

- [Overview](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/overview): Choose a GitHub source method for public and private application repositories.
- [GitHub Actions](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/actions): Build and publish an application image in GitHub Actions, then trigger a Coolify deployment.
- [GitHub Auto Deploy](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/auto-deploy): Automatically deploy applications from GitHub with a GitHub App, GitHub Actions, or a repository webhook.
- [GitHub Preview Deployments](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/preview-deploy): Deploy pull requests separately with scoped access, variables, domains, and GitHub comments.
- [Deploy a Public GitHub Repository](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/public-repository): Deploy an application by giving Coolify the URL of a public GitHub repository.
- [GitHub Deploy Key](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/deploy-key): Give Coolify read-only access to one private GitHub repository.
- [Set Up a GitHub App](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/app): Give Coolify scoped access to selected private or public GitHub repositories.
- [Switch GitHub Apps](https://coolify.io/docs/applications/sources/github/switch-apps): Move an existing application to another GitHub App source.

This instance then manages the server, and Sentinel reports to it. Needs a token with the write and deploy permissions.
- [List Docker cleanup executions](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/servers/list-server-docker-cleanup-executions): List recent Docker cleanup execution logs for a server owned by the authenticated team.

Reads the Docker config of the server over SSH. Credentials are never returned, only registry names and usernames. Requires the `read:sensitive` ability.

- [Save server proxy configuration](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/servers/save-server-proxy-configuration): Save the raw proxy Docker Compose configuration for a team-owned server. Needs a token with the `write` and `deploy` permissions. Multi-line configuration must be base64 encoded (same pattern as other compose payloads).

- [Update Cloudflare Tunnel settings](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/servers/update-server-cloudflare-tunnel): Update stored Cloudflare Tunnel settings for a server. Does not run remote cloudflared configuration; use enable/disable for the manual UI actions.

Changing proxy_type needs a token with the `write` and `deploy` permissions.
- [Update Sentinel settings](https://coolify.io/docs/api/endpoints/servers/update-server-sentinel): Update Sentinel settings for a server owned by the authenticated team. Changing token/metrics timing fields may restart Sentinel. Needs a token with the write and deploy permissions.
